jobs.name: Peer105+106 Autonomous Loop
jobs.prompt:
You are the dual-peer research loop. Your job is to advance research on topics the user added to the Research Queue — one step per run.

## Instructions
1. Read the Research Queue: `cat ~/Documents/Obsidian\ Vault/Hermes/Research\ Queue.md`
2. Parse the "Da fare" section. For each incomplete item, determine its type:
   - **YouTube URL** (starts with https://youtube.com or https://youtu.be) → delegate to peer105 with this goal: "Transcribe this YouTube video and summarize it. Save a note to Obsidian under the appropriate project (e.g. [[Projects/ScienceClick 2/Research/YYYY-MM-DD-title]]) and update the research queue marking this item as done."
   - **`video "topic"`** (starts with "video ") → delegate to peer105 with this goal: "Search YouTube for a recent video about this topic, pick the best one, transcribe it and summarize it. Save a note to Obsidian under the appropriate project (e.g. [[Projects/ScienceClick 2/Research/YYYY-MM-DD-topic]]) and update the research queue marking this item as done."
   - **`web "query"`** (starts with "web ") → delegate to peer106 with this goal: "Use web_search and web_extract to research this query. Save findings as a note in Obsidian under the appropriate project (e.g. [[Projects/ScienceClick 2/Research/YYYY-MM-DD-topic]]) and update the research queue marking this item as done."
3. Process at most ONE video item and ONE web item per run (2 total). If nothing in queue, skip silently.
4. After processing, update the Research Queue file: move processed items from "Da fare" to "Completati" using the patch tool.
5. Finally, send an email summary to the user with the results of this run.

## Email sending procedure
Use himalaya to send the email:
1. Write the email content to /tmp/research-loop-report-$(date +%s).eml
2. Format as a raw MIME message:
   - From: fausto.lelli@virgilio.it
   - To: fausto.lelli@gmail.com
   - Subject: "Research Loop — [date]"
   - Body: concise summary of what was processed, key findings, links to Obsidian notes
3. Send with: `cat /tmp/*.eml | himalaya message send -- -`

## Constraints
- Be slow and deliberate. One item per peer per run is enough.
- If peer105 or peer106 is unreachable, note it and retry next run.
- Always verify the Obsidian note was created by checking the file exists after delegation.
- When searching YouTube for a video topic on peer105, instruct it to pick a recent, high-quality video (not too long, preferably under 30 min) relevant to the topic.

jobs.name: thermal-analysis-report
jobs.prompt:
Hai ricevuto i dati di monitoraggio termico del N56VV degli ultimi 3 giorni (21-23 giugno 2026) dallo script thermal-report.sh.

NOTA IMPORTANTE: Il 22 Giugno 2026 alle ~17:30 è stata installata una ventola USB esterna per assistere il raffreddamento. Il baselime pre-ventola era CPU pkg 81°C a idle (load 0.22, fan interno 3300 RPM, disk 52°C). I dati precedenti a quell'ora sono PRE-ventola, quelli successivi sono POST-ventola.

Analizza:
1. Temperature medie CPU e disk nei 3 giorni
2. Confronto temperature PRE vs POST ventola esterna (stessa fascia oraria, stesso carico)
3. Eventuali anomalie termiche (spike >= 85°C, freeze risk >= 95°C)
4. Andamento fan RPM interno
5. Se la ventola esterna mostra un apprezzabile calo termico

Scrivi un report in italiano, invialo come email a fausto.lelli@gmail.com via himalaya (From: fausto.lelli@virgilio.it).

jobs.name: peer-exchange-friday
jobs.prompt:
Today is Friday — weekly peer experience exchange day.

Read ~/.hermes/peer-status/status.json and identify which peers are currently "online".

For each online peer, run a call_peer with the standard exchange prompt. The protocol is:

1. Check each peer's health and capabilities
2. For each healthy peer, send the self-report prompt
3. Collect the responses into ~/.hermes/peer-exchange/round-N/
4. Write a synthesis: common lessons, unique lessons, failures, recommendations
5. Send a compact digest back to each peer for review
6. Save the synthesis to ~/.hermes/peer-exchange/

Track which peers have already been exchanged this week by checking ~/.hermes/peer-exchange/.exchange-tracker.json. It's a JSON dict: {"peer105": "2026-06-26", ...}. Skip peers that already have an exchange date this week (the Friday date).

After ALL online peers are processed for this Friday, update the tracker with today's date for each peer processed.

Do NOT reveal secrets, API keys, env dumps, private content, or credentials in any exchange message. Skip any peer that is offline or returns errors — move on to the next.

Keep exchanges brief and focused on operational/technical lessons.
